newsitem.title: UK: British government seeks violent videos crackdown.
newsitem.headline: British government seeks violent videos crackdown.

text.p: The government on Tuesday demanded action by Britain's censors to curb video violence, saying people were justifiably concerned by films like "Natural Born Killers."
The call from interior minister Michael Howard was the latest move in a government campaign to crack down on crime and violence and promote family values.
Home Secretary Howard wrote to the British Board of Film Classification asking for a report on what action they are taking to reduce the level of violence.
Junior interior minister Tom Sackville told the British Video Association that 81 percent of households now had video recorders and industry sales totalled 789 million pounds ($1.30 billion) a year.
"With the large number of videos now being watched in the home we need to be sure that classification is working as well as it should," he said.

"Some classification decisions to allow videos like 'Natural Born Killers' and 'Executions - The Video', an 18 certificate, (allowing anyone of that age or above to buy or hire them) have caused widespread, and justified, public concern."
Criics said they were catalogues of gratuitous violence with no artistic merit.

"There is too much violence in videos. There is public concern about that. The video industry must take their share of responsibility for reducing the level of violence to which people are exposed," Sackville said.
National Heritage Secretary Virginia Bottomley has also written to the BBC and the governing body of independent television to seek their views on the issue of TV violence.

Howard's move follows a chorus of calls to make British society less violent. The demands were triggered by a series of horrific crimes, such as the Dunblane school massacre and the knifing to death of a headmaster outside his school.
The government has responded by introducing legislation to ban most handguns, impose heavier sentences on repeat offenders and give schools greater powers to discipline unruly pupils.
But oppositon parties have demanded a complete handgun ban and measures to curb the sale of combat knives.
